item.description: Thursday on the News Hour, former Prince Andrew is arrested as part of the widening global fallout related to Jeffrey Epstein. Nations pledge billions of dollars to President Trump's so-called Board of Peace that promises to rebuild war-torn Gaza. item.title: Say She She at WARSAW
item.description: Say She She at WARSAWFeb. 20. 7PM. $37.50+up The three singers who lead the group Say She She are all classically trained, but they all like different things: 70s style New York dance music, classic soul and R&B, the swirling psychedelia of Turkish pop or Hindi film music. Together they make a kind of post-disco pop that features an effortless but irresistible dance beat and the trio’s own rich and subtle vocal harmonies. item.title: American Dreams: Icons - The Moth Podcast
item.description: As America approaches it's 250th anniversary, we’ve decided to explore the American Dream - not just the singular American Dream, but all of them. Because our dreams contain multitudes. We’re dedicating our Spring Mainstage season, as well as some special podcast episodes, to exploring that theme. To kick that off, on this episode, we have two stories about American Iconography, but with a twist. This episode was hosted by Suzanne Rust. Storytellers: John Garcia and his father bond over bigfoot.

item.title: Niia at Blue Note
item.description: Niia at Blue NoteFeb. 23. 8PM and 10:30PM The singer Niia, born Niia Bertino, is a musical agent provocateur, who lures in jazz audiences with smoky versions of songs like “Angel Eyes” and even “The Christmas Song” and then hits them with her own dance-oriented, occasionally X-rated originals. As a songwriter Niia draws freely on soul, hip hop and rock, and she recently put out her fifth album of her own works. That album is simply called V, (the Roman numeral five).
